title: Geneva Rising
premise: Wendell Nystrom, a fixer for a deniable diplomatic unit in Geneva, has spent two years burying the memory of a botched extraction that left an informant dead. When a stranger named Ilse Varga repays a favor Wendell never performed—and demands interest in the form of a ledger proving her own agency orchestrated that death—Wendell is pulled into a hunt through Geneva's shadow diplomacy. As she and Ilse grow close, Wendell must decide whether to trade the ledger, the one secret worth killing for, to save Ilse's kidnapped brother. In the end, Wendell burns her own cover to expose the unit's director, choosing love and justice outside the law over the invisibility she once treasured.
about_author: Ulyana Blackwood is a former translator who spent a decade shuttling between Eastern European consulates before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people who keep other people's secrets, drawing on the gray corridors of international bureaucracy she knows too well.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Wendell Nystrom's POV. Insomniac Wendell works a routine cleanup job at a Geneva hotel, erasing a diplomat's indiscretion, when a stranger, Ilse Varga, intercepts her: 'You helped my family once. Now I'm calling it in.' Wendell has no memory of any such favor. The beat is unease—the past knocking on a door she sealed.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Ilse reveals a partial ledger implicating Wendell's own unit in the extraction that killed informant Tomas Reiner two years ago. She wants the rest of the ledger from the unit's archive; in exchange she'll vanish and take Wendell's name with her. Beat: dread mixed with a dangerous flicker of hope for answers.

chapters.title: House of Mirrors
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell reconnoiters the unit's archive beneath a fake trade mission on Rue de Lausanne, cataloguing security while pretending normalcy at morning briefing. Director Aldous Kray watches her too closely. Beat: paranoia tightening—she realizes someone may already suspect her.

chapters.title: The Brother
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse's motivation surfaces: her brother Marek, a courier who copied the full ledger, has gone missing in Lyon. Flashbacks show how she traced Wendell through a debt of gratitude their father recorded before his death. Beat: fierce, guilt-driven resolve.

chapters.title: Two Years of Bad Sleep
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A flashback chapter: the botched extraction in Trieste, Tomas Reiner's death, and the order Wendell obeyed to erase all traces—including her own report. Present-day Wendell decides to help Ilse, telling herself it's only to learn the truth. Beat: grief finally given permission to speak.

chapters.title: Dead Drop on the Pont de la Machine
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. First operational move: Wendell copies an access key during a staged fire alarm. Her colleague and sometime lover, analyst Petra Lindqvist, covers for her—then asks one question too many. Beat: intimacy fraying under secrecy.

chapters.title: Lyon, After Midnight
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wendell and Ilse trace Marek's last known route through Lyon's silk-worker district, finding his safehouse tossed and a surveillance photo of him in custody. They realize a rival service, not their own, took him. Beat: the conspiracy grows larger than either woman imagined.

chapters.title: Kray's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Director Kray invites Wendell to dinner and offers her a promotion—to 'legacy management,' cleaning up old operations like Trieste. It's a test, a bribe, and a threat in one. Beat: vertigo; the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse decodes the partial ledger and finds Wendell's name listed not as perpetrator but as the operative who tried to stop the kill order. Her hatred of the agency softens into something more complicated toward its messenger. Beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: Petra's Question
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Petra confronts Wendell with evidence of the archive breach—not to betray her, but because Petra lost a friend in Trieste too. An uneasy alliance forms inside the walls. Beat: betrayal inverted into solidarity.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Word reaches Wendell that the full ledger will be sold at a discreet auction among intelligence brokers in a Zurich private bank. Kray intends to buy and burn it. Wendell must get there first. Beat: the race begins, clock audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Marek
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse receives proof of life: a video of Marek, beaten, reciting a phrase only he and she know. The ransom demand isn't money—it's the ledger. The kidnappers are Kray's contractors. Beat: horror crystallizing into cold clarity.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell calculates the impossible math: one ledger, two demands—Ilse needs it to free Marek, the auction buyers want it destroyed, and Wendell needs it to indict Kray. She proposes a forgery. Beat: desperate ingenuity.

chapters.title: The Copyist
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra uses archival privileges to fabricate a convincing duplicate ledger, seeding it with one true page as verification. The act makes her a traitor beyond redemption. Beat: quiet terror and unexpected liberation.

chapters.title: Zurich, Vault Seven
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The auction: Wendell infiltrates the bank as a broker's aide, swaps the forged ledger into the lot, and comes face to face with Kray, who smiles as if he expected her. Beat: high-wire tension snapping into open confrontation.

chapters.title: Interest Collected
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. While Wendell holds Kray's attention, Ilse trades the real ledger's location to the kidnappers and extracts Marek herself, nearly dying in a stairwell ambush. Beat: ferocious courage; the siblings reunited but marked.

chapters.title: The Turn
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Kray reveals he knew about Wendell since chapter three—he let her run to find every loose thread, including Ilse and Marek. He offers her Tomas Reiner's death certificate signed by her own hand as leverage. Beat: the floor falling away; total exposure.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Branded a traitor, Wendell goes dark with Ilse's help, hiding in the Jura hills while the unit hunts them. Petra feeds them Kray's travel schedule from inside. Beat: fugitive calm before the storm; love confessed in whispers.

chapters.title: The One Secret Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell realizes the ledger alone won't destroy Kray—but her original suppressed Trieste report, still sealed in a Geneva notary vault, will. Retrieving it means walking into the unit's headquarters. Beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Rue de Lausanne, Last Entry
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Wendell returns to headquarters under Petra's credentials, retrieves the report, and triggers the building's audit alarms to force everything into official record. Kray corners her on the roof. Beat: climax—exposure as a weapon.

chapters.title: Geneva Rising
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Rather than kill her, Wendell lets Kray incriminate himself on a live wire tapped by an oversight committee Petra alerted; he's taken into custody by men even he can't fix. The unit begins to unravel publicly. Beat: catharsis—justice achieved outside every law they served.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue. Months later, Wendell lives under a new name near Lake Annecy with Ilse and Marek nearby. She testifies anonymously, visits Tomas Reiner's grave, and—for the first time in two years—sleeps until morning. Beat: quiet resolution; inheritance transformed into choice.
